newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PESO RECOVERY TO DRAW BACK MANILA GRAINS BUYERS.
newsitem.headline: PESO RECOVERY TO DRAW BACK MANILA GRAINS BUYERS.

text.p: The recovery of the peso is expected to lure back Philippine grains buyers into the market in the coming week, traders said on Friday.
"Hopefully, with cheaper dollars we can resume buying," an executive at a local flour mill told Reuters.

But a senior Manila grains trader said higher U.S. wheat prices due to El Nino fears in some countries, particularly China, and the prospect of Egypt going back into the wheat market would keep some buyers on the sidelines.
"It's scary to buy wheat at this time," the trader said.
A Philippine mill rejected tenders for the supply of 25,000 tonnes U.S. wheat for September shipment on Friday due to high prices.
Philippine firms stepped up wheat buying at the start of this month due to softer prices and the slight recovery of the peso, traders said.
Local flour millers bought 100,000 tonnes Canadian wheat and 67,000 tonnes U.S. wheat since August 1.
Philippine wheat buyers were mostly sidelined last month after the peso plunged by more than 11 percent following its de facto devaluation on July 11.
But the peso has been recovering in recent days. It closed at 28.51 on Friday compared to a low of 30 pesos soon after the devaluation.
